The '''2023–24 season''' was [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|120th season in existence]] and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time table|93rd consecutive season]] in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2023–24 La Liga|domestic league]], Real Madrid participated in this season's editions of the [[2023–24 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2024 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]] and the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

On the domestic front, Madrid delivered the Supercopa de España trophy, beating [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] 4–1 in the [[2024 Supercopa de España final|final]] to win their 13th title in the competition, and conquered a record-extending 36th La Liga championship with four games to spare.<ref name="Supercopa title">{{cite web|last=Drury|first=Sam|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Barcelona: Los Blancos win Spanish Super Cup with Vinícius Jr hat-trick|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67975415|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 January 2023|access-date=14 January 2023|archive-date=17 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240117065108/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67975415|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="La Liga title">{{cite web|title=Our 36th LaLiga title!|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/campeones-liga-2024-04-05-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=4 May 2024|access-date=4 May 2024|archive-date=4 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240504201210/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/campeones-liga-2024-04-05-2024|url-status=live}}</ref> These two trophies also marked [[Carlo Ancelotti]]'s 11th and 12th in charge of Real Madrid, overtaking [[Zinedine Zidane]]'s tally to make the Italian the [[List of Real Madrid CF managers#Trophies|second most successful]] manager in the club's history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ancelotti is now the second coach with the most titles in the history of Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/ancelotti-ya-es-el-segundo-entrenador-con-mas-titulos-en-la-historia-del-real-madrid-04-05-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=4 May 2024|access-date=6 May 2024|archive-date=6 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240506104302/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/ancelotti-ya-es-el-segundo-entrenador-con-mas-titulos-en-la-historia-del-real-madrid-04-05-2024|url-status=live}}</ref> In the Champions League, Madrid beat [[Borussia Dortmund]] 2–0 in the [[2024 UEFA Champions League final|final]] to a record-extending 15th European Cup, with [[Dani Carvajal]], [[Toni Kroos]], [[Luka Modrić]] and [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]] equalling [[Paco Gento]]’s record of six European Cup titles, as Ancelotti won his fifth trophy in the tournament, the most among the managers.<ref name="CL win">{{cite web|last=Pettit|first=Mark|title=Real Madrid win Champions League: Carvajal and Vinícius Júnior see off Dortmund|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/028e-1b07e18d875a-ba78e4b9d9fc-1000--report-madrid-win-champions-league/|publisher=UEFA|date=1 June 2024|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601213855/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/028e-1b07e18d875a-ba78e4b9d9fc-1000--report-madrid-win-champions-league/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Gento's record">{{cite web|title=Nacho, Modrić, Kroos and Carvajal have joined Gento in having won a record six European Cups|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/nacho-modric-kroos-y-carvajal-igualan-el-record-de-6-copas-de-europa-de-gento-01-06-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=1 June 2024|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604153341/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/nacho-modric-kroos-y-carvajal-igualan-el-record-de-6-copas-de-europa-de-gento-01-06-2024|url-status=live}}</ref> Real also claimed their fifth ever [[Double (association football)#European double|European double]] (after [[1956–57 Real Madrid CF season|1956–57]], [[1957–58 Real Madrid CF season|1957–58]], [[2016–17 Real Madrid CF season|2016–17]], and [[2021–22 Real Madrid CF season|2021–22]]). The team only suffered two defeats throughout the whole season, both of them against [[Madrid derby|city rivals]] [[Atlético Madrid]] at the [[Metropolitano Stadium|Cívitas Metropolitano]].

This season was the first since [[2008–09 Real Madrid CF season|2008–09]] to not feature [[Karim Benzema]], who departed to Saudi Arabian club [[Al-Ittihad Club (Jeddah)|Al-Ittihad]] and the first since [[2015–16 Real Madrid CF season|2015–16]] without [[Marco Asensio]], who left ''Los Merengues'' to join French side [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]].

==Summary==
===Pre-season===

Vicente|first1=Sergio|last2=Reidy|first2=Paul|title=Official: Marco Asensio to leave Real Madrid|url=https://en.as.com/soccer/official-marco-asensio-to-leave-real-madrid-n/|publisher=AS|date=3 June [[Mariano Díaz|Mariano]] and [[Eden Hazard]].<ref>{{cite web|title=OFFICIAL: Mariano Diaz leaves Real Madrid|url=https://www.managingmadrid.com/2023/6/3/23747996/official-mariano-diaz-leaves-real-madrid|publisher=Managing Madrid|date=3 June 2023|access-date=10 June 2023|archive-date=10 June spell|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/hazard-leave-real-madrid-after-dismal-four-year-spell-2023-06-03/|publisher=Reuters|date=3 June 2023|access-date=10 June 2023|archive-date=10 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230610123239/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/hazard-leave-real-madrid-after-dismal-four-year-spell-2023-06-03/|url-status=live}}</ref> The following day, Madrid announced an agreement with [[Karim Benzema]] for the club captain to depart in the summer after 14 years of service, with the Frenchman leaving the club as the joint-most decorated player in Real's history, having won 25 trophies.<ref>{{cite web|last=Romano|first=Fabrizio|author-link=Fabrizio Romano|title=Karim Benzema says goodbye to Real Madrid with goal in final On 9 June, Madrid confirmed the return of the former [[Real Madrid Castilla|club's academy]] player, [[Fran García (footballer, born 1999)|Fran García]], triggering the release clause to sign him from [[Rayo Vallecano]] on a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Fran García joins Real next day, Madrid announced that [[Brahim Díaz]] will be part of the first team for the 2023–24 season, additionally extending his contract until 2027.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Real Madrid tie Brahim Díaz to new contract until 2027|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4599044/2023/06/10/real-madrid-brahim-diaz-contract-2/|publisher=The ===August===
On 12 August, Madrid started their 2023–24 campaign with a 2–0 [[El Viejo Clásico]] win at the [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés]], beating [[Athletic Bilbao]] in the first matchday of [[2023–24 La Liga|La Liga]] with a strike from [[Rodrygo]] and Bellingham's debut goal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Athletic Bilbao 0–2 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores on his debut as Real win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66489759|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=12 August 2023|access-date=12 August 2023|archive-date=6 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230906092412/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66489759|url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, following [[Thibaut Courtois]]' [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL injury]], Madrid signed [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] as his replacement on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Courtois medical report|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/medical-reports/courtois-medical-report-10-08-2023|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=10 August 2023|access-date=14 August 2023|archive-date=7 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207214811/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/medical-reports/courtois-medical-report-10-08-2023/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Kepa is a new Real Madrid player|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/kepa-is-a-new-real-madrid-player|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=14 August 2023|access-date=14 August 2023|archive-date=7 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207211129/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/kepa-is-a-new-real-madrid-player/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 19 August, Madrid took on [[UD Almería|Almería]] on the road and managed to get a 3–1 win, thanks to a brace from Bellingham and a goal from [[Vinícius Júnior]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Almería 1–3 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/almer%C3%ADa-vs-real-madrid/FcR05x7OeloxkJWX/|publisher=The Athletic|date=19 August 2023|access-date=19 August 2023|archive-date=19 August Bellingham header helped Madrid to obtain a narrow 1–0 away win against [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] and continue their perfect league start.<ref>{{cite web|title=Celta Vigo 0–1 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/celta-de-vigo-vs-real-madrid/4pWaQ7rZVDbOayEB/|publisher=The Athletic|date=25 August 2023|access-date=25 August 2023|archive-date=25 August ===September===
On 1 September, the deadline day of the summer transfer window, [[Álvaro Odriozola]] returned to [[Real Sociedad]] on a permanent basis.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Odriozola|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/official-announcement-odriozola-01-09-2023|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=1 September 2023|access-date=2 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207210449/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/official-announcement-odriozola-01-09-2023/|url-status=live}}</ref> The following day, a close-range goal from Joselu and Bellingham's [[Association football#Duration and tie-breaking methods|injury time]] winner gave Ancelotti's side a 2–1 comeback win over [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] in their first league game of the season at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Getafe: Jude Bellingham scores fifth goal of season in injury time to rescue Real|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66696168|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=2 September 2023|access-date=2 September 2023|archive-date=4 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230904100059/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66696168|url-status=live}}</ref> After the [[FIFA International Match Calendar|international break]], on 17 September, second-half goals from [[Federico Valverde]] and Joselu earned Madrid a 2–1 home win over Real Sociedad, extending the team's winning run to five games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Real Sociedad|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-madrid-vs-real-sociedad/Rai5eXlWTDLw2OBS/|publisher=The Athletic|date=17 September 2023|access-date=17 September 2023|archive-date=19 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230919071344/https://theathletic.com/football/game/real-madrid-vs-real-sociedad/Rai5eXlWTDLw2OBS/|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, another late winner from Bellingham clinched Madrid a 1–0 win against [[1. FC Union Berlin|Union Berlin]] in the first matchday of the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rindl|first=Joe|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Union Berlin: Late Jude Bellingham winner beats Champions League debutants|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66871645|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=20 September 2023|access-date=20 September 2023|archive-date=20 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230920193117/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66871645|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 September, Ancelotti's side suffered their first defeat in the season, as the away [[Madrid derby]] match against [[Atlético Madrid]] ended in a 1–3 loss, with the team's only goal coming from Kroos.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlético Madrid 3–1 Real Madrid: Álvaro Morata scores twice as hosts win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66908689|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=24 September 2023|access-date=24 September 2023|archive-date=25 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925114153/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66908689|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid defeated [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] 2–0 at home, as Brahim and Joselu got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Las Palmas|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/las-palmas-vs-real-madrid/2QWdGQZQcqZD4qgN/|publisher=The Athletic|date=27 September 2023|access-date=27 September 2023|archive-date=27 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003213140/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66973253|url-status=live}}</ref>

===October===
On 3 October, finishes from Vinícius and Bellingham, as well as an own goal, got Madrid a 3–2 turnaround win over [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] at the [[Stadio Diego Armando Maradona]] in their second Champions League match of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jackson|first=Bobbie|title=Napoli 2–3 Real Madrid: Bellingham helps Los Blancos to entertaining victory in Naples|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66999126|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=3 October 2023|access-date=3 October 2023|archive-date=3 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231003213851/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66999126|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] was beaten 4–0 at home, thanks to a brace from Bellingham and goals from Vinícius and Joselu.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–0 Osasuna|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/osasuna-vs-real-madrid/MFtPUJBdWoY4j3dz/|publisher=The Athletic|date=7 October 2023|access-date=7 October 2023|archive-date=10 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231010122033/https://theathletic.com/football/game/osasuna-vs-real-madrid/MFtPUJBdWoY4j3dz/|url-status=live}}</ref> After another international break, Madrid returned to play on 21 October with a 1–1 away draw against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], as [[Dani Carvajal]] got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sevilla 1–1 Real Madrid: Sergio Ramos helps Sevilla hold his old team|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67184428|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=21 October 2023|access-date=21 October 2023|archive-date=23 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231023000816/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67184428|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid faced [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] away from home in the Champions League, beating the Portuguese side 2–1 with goals from Rodrygo and Bellingham.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rindl|first=Joe|title=Braga 1–2 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores in Champions League win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67209991|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=24 October 2023|access-date=24 October 2023|archive-date=24 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231024211807/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67209991|url-status=live}}</ref> On 28 October, Bellingham scored two goals to give Madrid a late 2–1 comeback victory over [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys|Olímpic Lluís Companys]] in the first [[El Clásico]] of the season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rindl|first=Joe|title=Barcelona 1–2 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores screamer and injury-time winner in El Clasico|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67251398|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=28 October 2023|access-date=28 October 2023|archive-date=28 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231028163121/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67251398|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Vinícius prolongated his agreement with the club through 2027.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Vinícius Júnior signs new Real Madrid contract to 2027|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5017061/2023/10/31/vinicius-jr-real-madrid-contract/|publisher=The Athletic|date=31 October 2023|access-date=31 October 2023|archive-date=31 October 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231031140104/https://theathletic.com/5017061/2023/10/31/vinicius-jr-real-madrid-contract/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===November===
On 2 November, Madrid announced that Rodrygo had renewed his contract until 2028.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Rodrygo signs new Real Madrid contract until 2028|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5018222/2023/11/02/rodrygo-real-madrid-contract/|publisher=The Athletic|date=2 November 2023|access-date=2 November 2023|archive-date=2 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231102135421/https://theathletic.com/5018222/2023/11/02/rodrygo-real-madrid-contract/|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid's home game versus Rayo Vallecano ended in a 0–0 stalemate.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 0–0 Rayo Vallecano: Jude Bellingham brushes off shoulder scare in La Liga draw|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67329281|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=5 November 2023|access-date=5 November 2023|archive-date=6 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231106024833/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67329281|url-status=live}}</ref> On 7 November, [[Eduardo Camavinga]] extended until 2029.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Eduardo Camavinga signs new Real Madrid contract to 2029|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5039507/2023/11/07/eduardo-camavinga-contract-real-madrid/|publisher=The Athletic|date=7 November 2023|access-date=7 November 2023|archive-date=7 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107193056/https://theathletic.com/5039507/2023/11/07/eduardo-camavinga-contract-real-madrid/|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Champions League goals from Brahim, Vinícius and Rodrygo qualified Madrid to the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase]], as Ancelotti's side defeated Braga 3–0 at the Santiago Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Braga: Vinícius Jr stars as Real reach Champions League knockouts|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67363047|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=8 November 2023|access-date=8 November 2023|archive-date=8 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108221918/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67363047|url-status=live}}</ref> On 9 November, Valverde signed a contract extension until 2029.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Federico Valverde signs new Real Madrid contract|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5045249/2023/11/09/federico-valverde-real-madrid-contract/|publisher=The Athletic|date=9 November 2023|access-date=9 November 2023|archive-date=9 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109172118/https://theathletic.com/5045249/2023/11/09/federico-valverde-real-madrid-contract/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 11 November, an early Carvajal goal and braces from Vinícius and Rodrygo gave Madrid a smashing 5–1 victory over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] at home.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 5–1 Valencia|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-madrid-vs-valencia/YzToEySXt4Z40yv7/|publisher=The Athletic|date=11 November 2023|access-date=11 November 2023|archive-date=11 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231111221109/https://theathletic.com/football/game/real-madrid-vs-valencia/YzToEySXt4Z40yv7/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 November, Madrid's away league game versus [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] ended in a 3–0 win with a Rodrygo brace and a goal from Bellingham.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cádiz 0–3 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores again as Real return to top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67538934|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 November 2023|access-date=26 November 2023|archive-date=26 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231126214756/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67538934|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid secured the first spot in their Champions League group with a 4–2 win against Napoli, as first-half strikes from Rodrygo and Bellingham were followed up by the debut goal from [[Real Madrid Castilla|Castilla]]'s [[Nico Paz]] and Joselu's close-range shot.<ref>{{cite web|last=Rindl|first=Joe|title=Real Madrid 4–2 Napoli: Jude Bellingham scores in Champions League win|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67571134|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=29 November 2023|access-date=29 November 2023|archive-date=30 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130195829/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67571134|url-status=live}}</ref>

===December===
Ancelotti's side started the month with a win, beating Granada 2–0 on 2 December, with goals from Brahim and Rodrygo.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Granada: Brahim Díaz and Rodrygo send Los Blancos top|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67603759|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=2 December 2023|access-date=3 December 2023|archive-date=2 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202201217/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67603759|url-status=live}}</ref> A week later, Madrid took on [[Real Betis]], but was unable to take three points, as Bellingham's goal gave his team a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Betis 1–1 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores as La Liga leaders are denied|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67661225|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=9 December 2023|access-date=12 December 2023|archive-date=11 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231211121301/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67661225|url-status=live}}</ref> On 12 December, a brace from Joselu and Ceballos' goal helped Madrid to get a 3–2 win over Union Berlin and a perfect result in the Champions League group stage for the third time in the club's history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Union Berlin 2–3 Real Madrid: Spanish side reach Champions League last 16 with 100% record|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67697632|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=12 December 2023|access-date=12 December 2023|archive-date=14 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231214012752/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67697632|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Madrid's last 2023 game at the Bernabéu ended in a 4–1 victory over [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], as Bellingham, Rodrygo, Brahim and Modrić got on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Villarreal: Jude Bellingham header helps host return to top of La Liga|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67744909|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 December 2023|access-date=17 December 2023|archive-date=17 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231217221511/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67744909|url-status=live}}</ref> On 21 December, a [[Lucas Vázquez]] header in injury time gave Madrid a 1–0 win over [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]] to end the year as the league leaders.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alavés 0–1 Real Madrid: Late Lucas Vázquez strike sends visitors into top spot|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67797358|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=21 December 2023|access-date=21 December 2023|archive-date=21 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231221223911/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67797358|url-status=live}}</ref> Eight days later, Ancelotti renewed his contract until 2026.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Official Announcement: Carlo Ancelotti signs contract renewal|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/official-announcement-carlo-ancelotti-signs-contract-renewal-29-12-2023|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=29 December 2023|access-date=29 December 2023|archive-date=29 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231229132118/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/official-announcement-carlo-ancelotti-signs-contract-renewal-29-12-2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

===January===
On 3 January, Madrid started off 2024 by beating [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] 1–0 at the Bernabéu, thanks to a late headed goal by [[Antonio Rüdiger]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Emons|first=Michael|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Mallorca: Antonio Rüdiger scores late winner for La Liga leaders|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67867732|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=3 January 2023|access-date=5 January 2023|archive-date=3 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240103205155/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67867732|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, goals from Joselu, Brahim and Rodrygo helped Madrid to get a 3–1 [[2023–24 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] win over [[Arandina CF|Arandina]] and progress to the round of 16.<ref>{{cite web|title=Arandina 1–3 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/arandina-vs-real-madrid/BJtB9unsHhI4gEpr/|publisher=The Athletic|date=6 January 2023|access-date=6 January 2023|archive-date=6 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240106223824/https://theathletic.com/football/game/arandina-vs-real-madrid/BJtB9unsHhI4gEpr/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 January, the first [[2024 Supercopa de España]] semi-final ended in favor of Real, as goals from Rüdiger, [[Ferland Mendy]] and Carvajal helped Madrid reach extra time, where a deflected header from Joselu and Brahim's long-range shot on an [[Empty net goal|empty net]] gave their team a 5–3 win over Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 5–3 Atlético Madrid: Real win Spanish Super Cup semi-final thriller|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67937493|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=10 January 2023|access-date=10 January 2023|archive-date=10 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240110221826/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/67937493|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, the Brazilian duo of Vinícius and Rodrygo scored all goals in Madrid's 4–1 victory over El Clásico rivals Barcelona, with the former getting his second career hat-trick to help Real conquer their 13th Spanish Super Cup title.<ref name="Supercopa title"/> On 19 January, two late goals in extra time from Atlético Madrid saw Ancelotti's side being eliminated from the Copa Del Rey 2–4 away, as one own goal and one from Joselu were not enough in a second loss at the [[Metropolitano Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68022816|title=Atlético Madrid 4–2 Real Madrid: Antoine Griezmann scores in cup derby thriller|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=19 January 2023|access-date=19 January 2023|archive-date=20 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240120004036/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68022816|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid won 3–2 after being down by two goals against Almería at half-time, with the goals coming from Bellingham and Vinícius, as well as a stoppage time winner by Carvajal.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dickinson|first=Adam|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2023-2024/real-madrid-v-almeria-la-liga-live_sto9975761/story.shtml|title=Real Madrid 3–2 Almería: Jude Bellingham tees up Dani Carvajal for late, late winner in stunning comeback|publisher=Eurosport|date=21 January 2023|access-date=21 January 2023|archive-date=21 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240121180934/https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2023-2024/real-madrid-v-almeria-la-liga-live_sto9975761/story.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> On 24 January, [[Éder Militão]] signed a contract extension until 2028.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cortegana|first=Mario|title=Éder Militão signs new Real Madrid contract until 2028|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5051174/2024/01/23/eder-militao-real-madrid-contract/|publisher=The Athletic|date=24 January 2024|access-date=24 January 2024|archive-date=23 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240123133601/https://theathletic.com/5051174/2024/01/23/eder-militao-real-madrid-contract/|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid beat Las Palmas 2–1 away, with a goal from Vinícius and a late winner by Tchouaméni.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68117640|title=Las Palmas 1–2 Real Madrid: Carlo Ancelotti's side come from behind again to go top|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=27 January 2023|access-date=27 January 2023|archive-date=27 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240127180635/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68117640|url-status=live}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, a brace from Joselu gave Madrid a 2–0 away victory over Getafe in the first game of the month.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/getafe-vs-real-madrid/XSaNq0Q6c6bp6Lix/|title=Getafe 0–2 Real Madrid|publisher=The Athletic|date=1 February 2024|access-date=1 February 2024|archive-date=6 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240206022718/https://theathletic.com/football/game/getafe-vs-real-madrid/XSaNq0Q6c6bp6Lix/|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, another match against Atlético Madrid ended in a 1–1 draw at the Bernabéu, as Brahim's first-half goal was cancelled out by a late equaliser.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68198550|title=Real Madrid 1–1 Atlético Madrid: Diego Simeone's side rescue late point at leaders|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=4 February 2024|access-date=4 February 2024|archive-date=1 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240501151554/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68198550|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 February, Madrid won 4–0 over Girona at home to strengthen their lead in the league, through goals from Vinícius and Rodrygo, as well as a brace from Bellingham.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Corrigan|first1=Dermot|last2=Ballús|first2=Pol|last3=Harris|first3=Thom|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5265453/2024/02/10/real-madrid-girona-la-liga-result-analysis/|title=Real Madrid 4 Girona 0: Vinícius Jr and Jude Bellingham star in dominant display|publisher=The Athletic|date=10 February 2024|access-date=11 February 2024|archive-date=10 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240210195908/https://theathletic.com/5265453/2024/02/10/real-madrid-girona-la-liga-result-analysis/|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, a wondergoal from Brahim was enough to beat Champions League round of 16 opponents [[RB Leipzig]] 1–0 in the first leg.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Emma|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68268572|title=RB Leipzig 0–1 Real Madrid: Brilliant Brahim Díaz strike earns Champions League first-leg win|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=13 February 2024|access-date=13 February 2024|archive-date=13 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213221257/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68268572|url-status=live}}</ref> On 18 February, Madrid was halted by Rayo Vallecano to a 1–1 draw away, with Joselu getting on the scoresheet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jurejko|first=Jonathan|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68332119|title=Rayo Vallecano 1–1 Real Madrid: Carlo Ancelotti's side drop points in La Liga title race|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=18 February 2024|access-date=19 February 2024|archive-date=19 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240219020523/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68332119|url-status=live}}</ref> Seven days later, Sevilla was defeated 1–0 at Bernabéu, courtesy of a late strike from Modrić.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68373528|title=Real Madrid 1–0 Sevilla: Luka Modrić scores superb late winner for La Liga leaders|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=25 February 2024|access-date=25 February 2024|archive-date=26 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240226231602/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68373528|url-status=live}}</ref>

===March===
The month started for Madrid with a 2–2 away draw against Valencia on 2 March, as Vinícius got a brace.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-madrid-vs-valencia/mftpK68igQiookk1/|title=Valencia 2–2 Real Madrid|publisher=The Athletic|date=2 March 2024|access-date=2 March 2024|archive-date=2 March 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240302233220/https://theathletic.com/football/game/real-madrid-vs-valencia/mftpK68igQiookk1/|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Vinícius scored his team's goal in the 1–1 home draw of the Champions League second leg against RB Leipzig, prevailing Madrid to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jurejko|first=Jonathan|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68482757|title=Real Madrid 1–1 RB Leipzig (agg 2–1): Vinícius Junior makes visitors pay for missed chances|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=6 March 2024|access-date=10 March 2024|archive-date=10 March 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240310210754/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68482757|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 March, Madrid beat Celta Vigo 4–0 at home, with strikes from Vinícius and Güler, a debut one for the Turk, as well as two own goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68530327|title=Real Madrid 4–0 Celta Vigo: Vinícius Jr and Arda Güler score in La Liga win|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=10 March 2024|access-date=10 March 2024|archive-date=10 March 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240310195302/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68530327|url-status=live}}</ref> Six days later, Madrid beat Osasuna 4–2 away, as Vinícius got on the scoresheet twice alongside Carvajal and Brahim.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/osasuna-vs-real-madrid/CD28TohLlWStGzrv/|title=Osasuna 2–4 Real Madrid|publisher=The Athletic|date=16 March 2024|access-date=16 March 2024|archive-date=16 March 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240316172342/https://theathletic.com/football/game/osasuna-vs-real-madrid/CD28TohLlWStGzrv/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 31 March, Madrid concluded the month at home with Rodrygo's brace sealing a 2–0 victory against Athletic Bilbao. The match also saw the return of Militão from his ACL injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/athletic-club-vs-real-madrid/SFuSxKJ58rAGUgCk/|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Athletic Bilbao|publisher=The Athletic|date=31 March 2024|access-date=31 March 2024|archive-date=31 March 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240331214449/https://theathletic.com/football/game/athletic-club-vs-real-madrid/SFuSxKJ58rAGUgCk/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===April===
On 9 April, Madrid opened the month with the first leg of the Champions League quarter-finals tie against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at home, as an own goal and strikes from Rodrygo and Valverde helped Real to end the match in a thrilling 3–3 draw.<ref>{{cite web|last=Matthews|first=Callum|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68765707|title=Real Madrid 3–3 Manchester City: Champions League quarter-final evenly poised after classic first leg|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=9 April 2024|access-date=9 April 2024|archive-date=9 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240409221456/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68765707|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, a lone goal from outside the box by Tchouaméni gave Madrid a 1–0 win at Mallorca.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68809437|title=Mallorca 0–1 Real Madrid: Aurelien Tchouaméni goal maintains La Liga title push|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=13 April 2024|access-date=13 April 2024|archive-date=13 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240413195850/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68809437|url-status=live}}</ref> On 17 April, Rodrygo's goal was enough to see Madrid hold Manchester City to a 1–1 draw at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]] in the second leg of the Champions League quarter-finals, sending the tie to extra time and ultimately penalty shootout, where Ancelotti's side prevailed 4–3 to book their place in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=McNulty|first=Phil|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68830107|title=Manchester City 1–1 Real Madrid (agg 4–4, 3–4 on pens): Spaniards through after shootout|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=17 April 2024|access-date=17 April 2024|archive-date=17 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240417220902/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68830107|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, Madrid managed to get a 3–2 victory over Barcelona at the Santiago Bernabéu with the help of goals from Vinícius and Vázquez and a stoppage time winner from Bellingham, sealing their third El Clásico win in a row this season, for the first time since [[1935–36 Madrid FC season|1935–36]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Jackson|first=Bobbie|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68869328|title=Real Madrid 3–2 Barcelona: Jude Bellingham scores late to seal El Clásico win|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=21 April 2024|access-date=21 April 2024|archive-date=21 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240421213031/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68869328|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 April, Madrid's away game against Real Sociedad ended in a 1–0 win, as Güler scored on his first La Liga start.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68909689|title=Real Sociedad 0–1 Real Madrid: Arda Güler scores as Real Madrid close in on title|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=26 April 2024|access-date=26 April 2024|archive-date=26 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240426225742/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68909689|url-status=live}}</ref> Four days later, a double from Vinícius earned Madrid a 2–2 away draw against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the first game of the Champions League semi-finals, which was the first ''[[Bayern Munich–Real Madrid rivalry|European Clásico]]'' for Real since the [[2017–18 Real Madrid CF season|2017–18]] encounter.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sanders|first=Emma|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68894025|title=Bayern Munich 2–2 Real Madrid: Vinícius Júnior scores twice as Real draw with Bayern|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=30 April 2024|access-date=30 April 2024|archive-date=30 April 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240430210824/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68894025|url-status=live}}</ref>

===May===
Madrid started the month with a home match against Cádiz on 4 May, as second-half goals from Brahim, Bellingham and Joselu gave Real a 3–0 win. This game also marked Courtois' first appearance of the season after recovering from his knee injuries.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 3–0 Cádiz|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/cádiz-vs-real-madrid/6sIdLjTLjLz4rVOF/|publisher=The Athletic|date=4 May 2024|access-date=4 May 2024|archive-date=4 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240504185822/https://theathletic.com/football/game/cádiz-vs-real-madrid/6sIdLjTLjLz4rVOF/|url-status=live}}</ref> On the same day, with Girona beating Barcelona 4–2, Madrid were crowned La Liga champions for the record-extending 36th time.<ref name="La Liga title"/> On 8 May, Madrid faced Bayern Munich in the reverse leg of the Champions League semi-finals at the Santiago Bernabéu. Trailing 0–1 in the 87th minute, a late brace from Joselu gave his team a 2–1 win in the match and 4–3 on aggregate to send Real to the [[2024 UEFA Champions League final|final]] for the sixth time in eleven years, knocking the German side out for the fourth time in a row.<ref>{{cite web|last=Emons|first=Michael|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68973021|title=Real Madird 2–1 Bayern Munich (agg: 4–3): Joselu scores twice to take Real into Champions League final|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=8 May 2024|access-date=8 May 2024|archive-date=8 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240508214557/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68973021|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, Madrid took on already-relegated Granada, winning 4–0, as García's debut goal for the club was followed up by a finish from Güler and a brace from Brahim.<ref>{{cite web|title=Granada 0–4 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/granada-vs-real-madrid/GqqOYMorPkUKzTTH/|publisher=The Athletic|date=11 May 2024|access-date=11 May 2024|archive-date=11 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240511183302/https://theathletic.com/football/game/granada-vs-real-madrid/GqqOYMorPkUKzTTH/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 May, an early opener from Bellingham with Vinícius' brace and goals from Valverde and Güler gave Ancelotti's side a crushing 5–0 win over Alavés, as Madrid kept a club record 20th clean sheet in this La Liga campaign.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid 5–0 Alavés|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/deportivo-alavés-vs-real-madrid/fB8RzKeN7ZUzzSsg/|publisher=The Athletic|date=14 May 2024|access-date=14 May 2024|archive-date=14 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240514221506/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/deportivo-alav%C3%A9s-vs-real-madrid/fB8RzKeN7ZUzzSsg/|url-status=live}}</ref> Five days later, Madrid gave up a three-goal lead away to Villarreal at the [[Estadio de la Cerámica]], the match ending in a 4–4 draw, with goals from Vázquez, Joselu, and a double from Güler.<ref>{{cite news|title=Villarreal 4–4 Real Madrid|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-madrid-vs-villarreal/DpltLAxOd7wtN5Mh/|publisher=The Athletic|date=19 May 2024|access-date=19 May 2024|archive-date=19 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240519215516/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/game/real-madrid-vs-villarreal/DpltLAxOd7wtN5Mh/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 May, in the season's last league game, Madrid drew Real Betis 0–0, as Kroos bid a farewell to the Bernabéu.<ref>{{cite web|last=Thomas|first=Marissa|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c722zng14j5t|title=Real Madrid 0–0 Betis: Kroos gets Bernabéu send off as Real draw with Betis|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=25 May 2024|access-date=25 May 2024|archive-date=26 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240526073926/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c722zng14j5t|url-status=live}}</ref>

===June===
Madrid's only game of the month and their last match of the season was the Champions League final at the [[Wembley Stadium]] against [[Borussia Dortmund]]. A header from Carvajal and a strike from Vinícius late in the second half prevailed ''Los Blancos'' to a 2–0 win, as they clinched a record-extending 15th European Cup, their sixth in eleven years, Ancelotti's third in charge and fifth overall, the most among the managers, with Carvajal, Kroos, Modrić and Nacho equalling [[Paco Gento]]’s record of six European Cup titles and surpassing the former trio consisting of [[Karim Benzema]], [[Gareth Bale]], and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref name="CL win"/><ref name="Gento's record"/> Additionally, Modrić and Nacho won their 26th title in Real Madrid to become the players with the most trophies in the history of the club, surpassing Benzema and [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nacho and Modrić, 26 trophies with Real Madrid|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/nacho-y-modric-25-titulos-con-el-real-madrid-04-05-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=1 June 2024|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240601225808/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/nacho-y-modric-25-titulos-con-el-real-madrid-04-05-2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 13 May 2023, Real Madrid announced they would travel to the United States to participate in the pre-season Soccer Champions Tour for the second time since last year's summer activity.<ref>{{cite web|title=Real Madrid will play the Soccer Champions Tour 2023 this summer|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/real-madrid-will-play-the-soccer-champions-tour-2023-this-summer|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=12 May 2023|access-date=25 May 2023|archive-date=7 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207214754/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/real-madrid-will-play-the-soccer-champions-tour-2023-this-summer/|url-status=live}}</ref>
